case_title: P. Chidambaram v. Directorate of Enforcement
statutory_provisions: PMLA s.3 and 4; Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 s.8 and 13(2) r/w. s.13(1)(d); IPC s.120B r/w. s.13(1)(d)
trial_court_outcome: High Court dismissed the application for the grant of anticipatory bail
neutral_facts: The case involves allegations of irregularities in the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) clearance given to a company for receiving foreign investment, which was significantly higher than the approved inflow. The appellant was the then finance minister. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) registered a First Information Report (FIR) against the appellant and other accused persons under various sections of the Indian Penal Code and the Prevention of Corruption Act. The Enforcement Directorate also registered a case under sections 3 and 4 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. The High Court dismissed the application for the grant of anticipatory bail filed by the appellant, holding it to be a classic case of money laundering. The appellant appealed, seeking to produce materials collected during the investigation in a sealed cover for the Supreme Court to review. The Court accepted the submission of the respondent for the limited purpose of refusing pre-arrest bail to the appellant, but refrained from opening the sealed cover to avoid prejudice to the appellant and co-accused.
